gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the lithium trolling batteries in these sets stop taking a charge below 32°F and only start again above 41°F (Redodo's 12V, 24V and 36V trolling packs). That means a boat on an onboard charger in a cold garage or slip in November can sit plugged in all night and stay empty. The fix that decides the set is a self-heating pack (Redodo Apex Mini 24V 125Ah, which uses charger power to heat itself and charges down to -4°F) paired with a matched 29.2V charger, not a 12V multi-bank charger.
standout_why: I compared against the Minn Kota pages ChatGPT cited or received. 'Lithium Battery Selection and Recommendations' (cited) covers the BMS limiting current, motor voltage limits and charge profile but says nothing about low temperature, and nothing about balancing or series wiring. 'Charging Lithium Batteries' (a result, not cited) says Minn Kota chargers are 'not compatible with single 24V and 36V Lithium Batteries' and gives the 14.5V maximum, but again says nothing about temperature. 'Battery Charger Selection Guide' (a result) says the chargers are 12V-only and that series-wired batteries can't be charged on one bank. So the warning that a single 24V/36V battery needs its own 29.2V/43.8V charger is already partly in the results, and I'm not using it as the new fact. The low-temperature charge cutoff, and the heated pack that gets around it, appear in none of them. ChatGPT's own answers show a 'LiTime 24V 100Ah ... Low-Temp Cut…' card but never explain what that does to overnight charging. They also pair 2× 12V batteries with a 'NOCO Genius 2-Bank 10-Amp (5-Amp Per Bank)' card, which is the slow 12V-bank route, and never match a charger to their recommended single 24V or 36V battery. I couldn't open the Dakota Lithium or West Marine results this session, so I can't rule out that one of them mentions cold charging. That's why I scored 2, not 3.
kit_items: Battery (24V motor, cold-season or northern angler): Redodo Apex Mini 24V 125Ah LiFePO4. Redodo says it is self-heating, charges down to -4°F, has Bluetooth and is IP67. One battery means no series jumpers, and it doesn't stall on the low-temp cutoff like the other packs here.

Battery (24V motor, warm-climate alternative): Redodo 24V 100Ah Group 31 Bluetooth. It's cheaper but has the 32°F/41°F charge cutoff, and Redodo says it fits Group 31 trays but not standard Group 31 battery boxes.

Charger (24V): Redodo 29.2V 20A MINI LiFePO4 charger. It is the correct charge voltage for one 25.6V pack. A Minn Kota PCL or other 12V multi-bank charger can't charge a single 24V lithium battery (Minn Kota says so).

Battery + charger (36V motor, budget): Redodo 36V 50Ah + Redodo 43.8V 25A IP65 charger. The weak point is the 50A BMS (60A for 30 min, per Redodo), so check it against the motor's max amp draw before choosing it for a 36V motor at high thrust.
Battery + charger (12V kayak or jon boat): Redodo 12V 100Ah trolling battery with low-temp cutoff + Redodo 14.6V 20A charger.
Not in any of these carts: circuit breaker and marine wire. Redodo doesn't sell them in the store search I ran; size them from Minn Kota's chart for the specific motor.
